dharana.numbering_edition: Jaideva Singh 1979 (dhāraṇā 1 = verse 24; dhāraṇā 82 = verses 105–106 and dhāraṇā 89 = verses 113–114, otherwise one verse each; dhāraṇā 112 = verse 137)
dharana.sanskrit_iast: anāgatāyāṃ nidrāyām praṇaṣṭe bāhyagocare | sāvasthā manasā gamyā parā devī prakāśate ||
dharana.sanskrit_source: GRETIL e-text, compared with Wallis's concordance, Pradīpaka and the Singh scan
dharana.rendering: When sleep has not yet come but the outer world has faded away, that state can be reached by the mind; there the supreme Goddess shines.
dharana.rendering_attribution: School paraphrase drawing on Jaideva Singh (1979), Christopher Wallis and Bettina Bäumer (as printed in Wallis's concordance); not a quotation.
dharana.commentary_note: Singh: the in-between state of sleep and waking is a thought-free (nirvikalpa) state, which he identifies with the fourth (turīya), transcendental state; concentrating on it one experiences the nature of the Self, called here parā devī. Wallis: 'on the edge of sleep'.
dharana.instruction: As you fall asleep, notice the quiet edge just before sleep and rest there.

seat.label: Any steady, comfortable position (school addition)
seat.summary: Lying down as for sleep, which is where this threshold naturally occurs.
seat.honesty: School addition. Verse 75 does not specify a body position. The seat is a convenience so the dharana can be practised; it is not part of the technique and makes no claim of tradition.

points: waking, with the outer world fading
geometry.summary: Not a body shape. The map is a threshold in time: the outer world has faded, sleep has not yet come, and attention rests on the edge.
geometry.svg_hint: a line fading from light to dark with a thin bright band at the boundary
geometry.honesty: Geometry records the dharana's own map of attention, not a body shape. Locations marked 'commentarial' come from commentary, not from the verse.

reaction.name: Stay on the edge
reaction.summary: School metaphor only: the busy waking mind fades and, before sleep, a clear quiet edge is noticed. Not a biochemical or medical claim.

breath.lands_in: wherever the breath naturally ends; this door places nothing on the breath
breath.cue: Natural breath. Count about four in and four out only if it helps you settle, then let the count go. No forced hold.
breath.honesty: The counts are an optional school pacing aid, not part of the verse. Hold is always 0: this school never adds a deliberate breath-hold.

orientation.cue: Rest on the edge between waking and sleep
orientation.gravity: Let the floor or chair carry the body completely; there is no posture to hold
orientation.degrees_hint: No angle target: the VBT gives no posture for this dharana

attention.primary: The threshold where the outer world has faded and sleep has not yet come

adiyogi.verse_paraphrase: When sleep has not yet come but the outer world has faded away, that state can be reached by the mind; there the supreme Goddess shines.
adiyogi.method_summary: Lie down as for sleep. As the outer world fades, notice the quiet state just before sleep arrives. Rest attention lightly on that edge. If you fall asleep, that is fine.

honesty.disclosure: Door 052 follows Vijñāna Bhairava Tantra dharana 52 (verse 75) in Jaideva Singh's numbering. The door-to-dharana index is a School of 112 Doorways teaching device. Singh's sequence is one edition's count, not an ancient one-to-one canon. The seat, counts, reaction and beat scripts are school additions.
honesty.notes: pairing_type is school_device: the dharana is the content, while the door index, seat and pacing are the school's.
flags: Door index = Jaideva Singh dharana number: Door 052 is dharana 52, verse 75. Other editions number differently (see dharana.numbering_variants).
The seat, breath counts, reaction metaphor, attention-map drawing and beat scripts are school devices, not part of the verse.
The English is a school paraphrase, not a quotation from any translator.
No medical claims. Reaction names are metaphors, not biochemistry.

safety.pain_rule: Pain is information. Pause, regress, or exit. Never push through sharp pain.
safety.open_seat_alternate: This door needs no particular posture: sit on a chair, sit on the floor with support, or lie down. Eyes may stay open.
safety.contraindication_notes: General practice caution only; not medical advice. Let sleep come if it comes; do not keep yourself awake on purpose. If anything feels distressing (dizziness, agitation, strong emotion), stop, open the eyes and rest attention on the feet and the floor.
